title: Tanzanian Sweet Mandazi
community: Tanzania — the enriched sweet version of the everyday mandazi
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mandazi Tamu — the enriched, sweeter, softer dessert mandazi. Made with coconut milk, extra sugar, double cardamom, and an egg for richness — fried until deeply golden and dusted with icing sugar. The elevated version of Tanzania's everyday doughnut.
longDesc: Mandazi Tamu is what the everyday mandazi becomes when it is made for special occasions — more sugar, coconut milk instead of water, an extra egg, and double the cardamom. The result is a richer, softer, more fragrant doughnut that is genuinely a dessert rather than just a breakfast.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, cardamom, nutmeg, and salt.
Beat eggs into warm coconut milk. Add melted butter.
Combine wet and dry. Mix to a soft, slightly tacky dough.
Knead 5 minutes until smooth. Rest covered 60 minutes.
Roll to 1.5cm thickness. Cut into triangles or circles.
Fry at 170°C for 4 minutes per side until deeply golden.
Dust generously with icing sugar while still warm.
chefTips: Double the cardamom of a street mandazi — this is a dessert.
Coconut milk only — no water — for the richest result.
The icing sugar must go on while still warm so it adheres.
commonMistakes: Dusting icing sugar on cold mandazi — it slides off.
cookingScience: See TZA007 for mandazi cooking science. The additional egg in Sweet Mandazi adds lecithin — an emulsifier that helps the fat (coconut milk and butter) distribute more evenly throughout the dough, producing a more uniformly tender, richer crumb.
sustainabilityTips: Coconut milk from coastal Tanzanian palms.
storage: Best fresh. Store 2 days. Freeze 2 months.
reheating: Warm in oven at 150°C. Re-dust with icing sugar.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as an occasional treat.
culturalNote: Sweet mandazi is the mandazi that mothers make when they want to show their family they have taken extra care — the special occasion version of the everyday doughnut, distinguished by the extra sugar, the coconut milk, and the cloud of icing sugar that announces it is something different.
